title: Cognition stays asynchronous to live order execution
statement: The Superintelligence/cognition plane (latent state, forecasts, agents, twins, routing) must remain asynchronous to live order execution: no execution-path crate may depend on a cognition crate, and the fastest path stays regional and deterministic.
rationale: Planes are separated by latency/consistency need; cognition inserted synchronously into execution would make order timing depend on elastic, failure-prone services.

verification.check: A dependency-graph walk from every edge/reflex crate finds no cognition, language-model or solver crate; adding such an edge to qip-edge's Cargo.toml must fail the test.

title: Reflex plane on dedicated C4D/C4 Compute Engine VMs
statement: Reflex Execution must run on dedicated Compute Engine C4D/C4-class VMs with direct venue sessions, local books/features/models/risk, and no service-mesh or database dependency.
rationale: Lowest jitter and direct venue sessions; a mesh or DB hop in the decision loop adds unexplainable latency and a shared failure.

verification.check: terraform plan with a declared execution node shows a google_compute_instance_group_manager on a c4/c4d shape with no load balancer or mesh; a C3 or N2 shape must be refused at plan.

title: Reflex Mesh is direct peer QUIC between regional cells
statement: Regional Reflex Cells must coordinate 2–20-leg opportunities over a direct peer-to-peer QUIC mesh that is bounded and ephemeral by design.
rationale: Fast bounded multi-region coordination without routing through durable messaging or the centre.

verification.check: Two cells exchange a multi-leg proposal over the peer link within a bounded deadline; replacing the transport with a durable relay or dropping the bound must fail the test.

notes: QUIC needs a crate (e.g. quinn) — ADR 0002/0009 permit serde/serde_json only.

title: Fabric runs on dedicated Rust broker VMs per region
statement: The Rust Event & Control Fabric must run as dedicated Rust broker VMs in each region, providing one native contract for durable pub/sub, journals, replay, backpressure, control and outcomes.
rationale: One native contract replaces Pub/Sub/Kafka so semantics are owned in-tree.

verification.check: Each production region's plan contains broker instances running qip-fabricd; removing the module instantiation must fail the infrastructure acceptance test.

title: Regional Service Plane on regional GKE Standard
statement: Elastic warm services (asset/risk/capital, evidence, replay, fabric sinks, APIs, package distribution) must run on a regional GKE Standard service plane.
rationale: Warm services scale independently of the Reflex and Fabric planes.

verification.check: A plan shows a regional GKE Standard cluster per execution region hosting the warm services.

notes: KUBERNETES: conflicts with ADR 0024 (Cloud Run + Compute Engine). Intent (independently scaled warm services) can be met on Cloud Run.

title: Data/Intelligence plane on GCS, Bigtable, BigQuery, Catalog, Spanner Graph
statement: Pass-through world sensing, retained tick/internal history, compact provenance/knowledge, research and models must be served by GCS, Bigtable, BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, Spanner Graph and Agent Platform/Vertex APIs.
rationale: Each store is matched to an access pattern; one store for everything couples analytics to execution.

verification.check: Plan provisions each store and an in-tree adapter opens it; an adapter refusing the target must fail the integration test.

title: Financial truth in Spanner Enterprise Plus
statement: Ledger, positions, obligations, capital grants and idempotent outcome processing must live in a strongly consistent Spanner Enterprise Plus database as the financial system of record.
rationale: Financial truth needs external consistency and must not share fate with analytics.

verification.check: A ledger write commits through a Spanner adapter in one transaction; pointing the writer at a non-Spanner store in production config must be refused.

title: Engineering plane: Cloud Build pools, Artifact Registry, GitOps controllers
statement: The engineering/control plane must provide an immutable supply chain and GitOps promotion via GitHub, Cloud Build private pools, Artifact Registry, Config Sync and Argo CD/Kargo/Rollouts.
rationale: Immutable artefacts and declarative promotion make every production change reproducible and attributable.

verification.check: Images are built in a private pool, stored in Artifact Registry by digest and promoted only by Kargo/Argo commits; a manual deploy must be refused by policy.

notes: Config Sync / Argo need a cluster; ADR 0036 permits the GitOps control-plane cluster as the one Kubernetes exception.

title: No Pub/Sub or Managed Kafka in the internal runtime
statement: Google Pub/Sub and Managed Kafka must not be internal runtime dependencies for service-to-service control, tick journaling, outcomes or replay.
rationale: Algorik semantics are defined by the Rust fabric; a second bus would split them.

verification.check: No workspace crate declares a Pub/Sub/Kafka client and no Terraform grants publish/subscribe on a fabric topic; adding either must fail the scan.

title: Any Kafka/Pub/Sub partner bridge is stateless at the boundary
statement: If a partner requires Kafka/Pub/Sub compatibility, the bridge must be a stateless component at an external boundary and Algorik semantics must remain defined by the Rust fabric.
rationale: A stateful bridge becomes a second source of truth for event history.

verification.check: A bridge crate, if present, contains no durable-store type and nothing else depends on it; introducing DurableStore into it must fail.

title: External world payloads are transient and discarded after distillation
statement: External world content must be parsed, evidence-scored and distilled into durable knowledge, after which the source payload is discarded; GCP storage holds Algorik-created knowledge, not a mirror of the public world.
rationale: Mirroring sources raises cost and licensing/privacy exposure and makes a sealed log hold text that can never be removed.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: The durable record of an ingested document has no field able to hold source text; adding a body String to NewsItem must fail a structural test.

title: No default GCS landing bucket for external-world content
statement: Crawler/scout workers must stream source bytes through memory or encrypted ephemeral disk only; there must be no default GCS landing bucket for external-world content.
rationale: A landing bucket becomes a raw-world lake by default.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: No Terraform bucket is designated for external content; adding one must fail an acceptance scan.

title: Source manifest records the full re-fetch descriptor
statement: Each ingested source must have a manifest recording canonical URI/provider ID, retrieval time, version/etag, content hash, entitlement, cursor, freshness, parser lineage and re-fetch instructions.
rationale: Without the descriptor a discarded payload cannot be re-fetched or proven unchanged.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: Constructing a manifest without any of the nine fields is refused; dropping a field from the type must fail a round-trip test.

title: Source Manifest Registry persisted in Spanner/AlloyDB
statement: Source manifests must be held in a queryable Source Manifest Registry backed by Spanner or AlloyDB.
rationale: A manifest only embedded in events cannot be queried to drive re-fetch or freshness.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: A registry write and lookup by canonical URI round-trips through the Spanner/AlloyDB adapter.

title: Knowledge graph holds entities, edges, beliefs — never copied documents
statement: The knowledge graph (Spanner Graph, tier K1) must store entities, relationships, temporal facts, causal edges, source references, beliefs, confidence and contradictions, and never copied documents.
rationale: Durable knowledge must be Algorik's interpretation, not a corpus copy.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: Graph node/edge schema has no document-body field and a write of a copied document is refused.

notes: Merges §2.1 'Knowledge Graph' bullet and §9.2 Tier K1.

title: Bigtable holds fast derived knowledge state
statement: High-rate derived features, entity/event state, ambient-model state and time-indexed knowledge deltas must be stored in Bigtable.
rationale: Hot derived state needs a wide-column store distinct from the ledger and the graph.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: Feature/state deltas written via a Bigtable adapter are read back by time index.

title: Knowledge packs in GCS with lifecycle tiers
statement: Compact Algorik-derived knowledge packs (protobuf/Parquet snapshots, embeddings, summaries, world-model deltas, model artifacts) must be stored in GCS under Standard/Nearline/Coldline lifecycle tiers (tier K2).
rationale: Derived packs are far smaller than source corpora and can be tiered cheaply.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: Plan shows a pack bucket with lifecycle transitions; a pack writer stores only derived artifacts.

notes: Parquet/protobuf encoders would need new crates (ADR 0002).

title: Historical world analysis re-fetches via manifest, never copies
statement: Historical world analysis must re-fetch from the authoritative source/provider using the manifest and process transiently; licensed historical APIs are queried on demand instead of copying corpora.
rationale: Copying a provider corpus breaches licence and recreates the raw lake.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: A replay of a past document triggers a manifest-driven re-fetch whose hash is compared with the manifest; a cached copy path must not exist.

title: Tick and internal financial data are separate retained classes (Tier T)
statement: Tick/order-book data and Algorik-owned financial/execution data must be distinct retention classes, archived (GCS/Tick Lake) under entitlements when rights/policy require replay, accounting, audit or training.
rationale: Retained classes must not be confused with transient world data or each other.

sources.section: §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

verification.check: Each topic maps to exactly one retention class; tick and financial classes differ and archive with entitlement labels.

notes: Merges §2.1 tick bullet and §9.2 Tier T.

title: Hot path owns its dependencies: tick to order is local only
statement: Between tick and order only local process memory, local deterministic risk, local session state and the venue adapter may be used — no GKE, Spanner, Bigtable, Redis, AI endpoint or fabric acknowledgement.
rationale: Any remote dependency in the decision loop turns its outage or latency into an execution failure.

verification.check: Dependency-graph tests show no edge crate reaches storage, LM, solver or transport for lane-0 stages; adding qip-storage to qip-edge must fail.

title: Durable async work runs after or beside the reflex decision
statement: Control, outcomes, journals and telemetry must be durable where required but executed after or beside the reflex decision, never in front of it.
rationale: Async does not mean unimportant, but it must not gate the decision.

verification.check: A stalled journal destination does not delay a pass; removing the async boundary must fail the test.

title: One internal event model with mandatory envelope fields
statement: Every asynchronous event must carry event_id, producer_epoch, schema_id/version, region, logical timestamp, source timestamp, trace_id, ordering key, integrity checksum and provenance metadata.
rationale: Without these fields events cannot be deduplicated, ordered, traced or attributed after the fact.

verification.check: Encoding then decoding an event preserves all ten fields; building one with any field empty is refused.

title: At-least-once with idempotency; no exactly-once claim
statement: The platform must not claim global exactly-once delivery; consumers must deduplicate using event IDs, partition sequence and fencing epochs.
rationale: Claimed exactly-once hides duplicate effects when a retry crosses a failure.

verification.check: Under random lost acks, retries and restarts each sequence is appended once; a consumer replaying from an offset produces no duplicate effect.

title: Financial writers enforce uniqueness transactionally
statement: Financial writers must enforce event uniqueness inside the same transaction that applies the effect.
rationale: An offset committed apart from its postings loses or doubles a fill across a crash.

verification.check: For any duplication/redelivery/crash schedule, balances equal one clean delivery; splitting the write batch must fail.

title: Loss of global cognition or another region cannot stop a healthy cell
statement: A healthy Reflex Cell must keep operating when global cognition or any other region is lost.
rationale: Regions fail independently; a central outage must not become a global trading stop.

verification.check: A cell with its mesh link severed keeps placing paper orders within its envelope; making the pass require the centre must fail.

title: Every dependency has a degradation envelope
statement: Each dependency of a Reflex Cell must have a declared degradation envelope stating how the cell behaves as that input ages or disappears.
rationale: An undeclared dependency fails in an undeclared way.

verification.check: Each capability in the degradation table has a freshness bound and multiplier; a capability with no row must be refused at configuration.

title: Durability is declared per topic class
statement: Control and outcome topics must get quorum durability, telemetry may be sampled/dropped, and research streams optimise throughput, each declared per topic.
rationale: One durability for all topics either over-pays for telemetry or under-protects money.

verification.check: Declaring a P0/P1 stream with an ack profile below Quorum is refused; P4 admits None.

title: Caches own nothing authoritative
statement: Caches (including Memorystore Redis) must never hold authoritative state; loss of a cache causes rebuild or degraded latency, never lost financial state.
rationale: A cache treated as truth loses money silently when evicted.

verification.check: Every composition root resolving a storage target refuses a cache as store of record; resolving Memorystore as key_value must fail.

notes: Merges rule 7's cache clause and §9.2 Memorystore row.

title: Explicit state ownership across Spanner, Fabric, GCS, Bigtable
statement: State ownership must be explicit: Spanner owns financial truth; the Fabric owns event history/offsets; GCS owns retained archives and derived knowledge artifacts; Bigtable owns hot derived features; external payloads are transient.
rationale: Two owners of one fact disagree and the louder is wrong.

verification.check: Each fact class maps to one store in code; a second writer of the same class must fail an architecture test.

title: Deployments by signed immutable digests only
statement: Git and signed image digests must be deployment truth: no mutable tags are deployed.
rationale: A policy that trusts a tag trusts whoever can push it.

verification.check: Binary Authorization requires an attestation and workflows deploy by digest; a tag-only reference must be refused.

title: No secret values in Git
statement: No secret value may be committed to Git.
rationale: A committed secret is a leaked secret for the life of the history.

verification.check: check-secrets.sh over the tree and history reports nothing; committing a key fixture must fail CI.

title: No console-only changes or hand-copied models
statement: Production state must not be changed through console-only actions, and models must not be hand-copied into production.
rationale: Out-of-band changes are not reproducible from Git.

verification.check: Drift detection (plan) shows no unmanaged change; model activation requires a registry-signed artifact.

title: Autonomous agents obey the same production pipeline
statement: Autonomous agents may create PRs, run experiments and diagnose incidents, but any production change they cause must pass tests, attestations, promotion policy and rollback like any other change.
rationale: An agent with a side door to production bypasses every control.

verification.check: Agent identities hold no deploy permission outside the pipeline; a direct deploy by the agent identity is refused.

title: Execution region and topology chosen by venue benchmarks
statement: Region and topology must be determined by venue-specific latency benchmarks; GCP regional execution must not be represented as exchange colocation.
rationale: Cloud latency has physics; an unmeasured region choice is a guess.

verification.check: Each declared execution region cites a measured venue RTT; a cross-region arrangement without a measured RTT is refused.

title: Three execution regions chosen by measurement
statement: Production must start with three execution regions (Americas, Europe, APAC), selected by venue RTT, market-data RTT, legal residency, machine series, Interconnect options and counterparty proximity.
rationale: Hard-coded regions ignore where venues and law actually are.

verification.check: A prod plan declares execution nodes in three regions with recorded selection rationale.

title: Per-region Reflex, Fabric and Service networks with collectors and egress
statement: Each execution region must have its own Reflex VPC, Fabric VPC, Service VPC/cluster, regional landing storage, regional observability collectors and controlled egress.
rationale: Per-region separation bounds blast radius.

verification.check: Plan per region shows the three networks, landing bucket, collector and NAT.

notes: 'Service VPC/GKE cluster' — KUBERNETES conflicts with ADR 0024; Cloud Run serves the service plane.

title: Global shared plane: build, ledger, research, registry, catalog, identity
statement: Management/build plane, multi-region ledger, global research data, model registry, Knowledge Catalog and identity/security services must be global/shared rather than per region.
rationale: Shared concerns duplicated per region drift.

verification.check: Plan shows these as single global resources.

title: Zonal failure tolerated by standby, cross-zone replicas, multi-zone plane
statement: A single-zone loss must be survived through a Reflex standby in another zone, Fabric RF3 partition replicas across zones, and a regional multi-zone service plane.
rationale: A zone outage is routine and must not stop trading or lose the journal.

verification.check: Killing one zone leaves the cell, fabric quorum and warm services serving.

title: Regional failure: healthy regions continue, critical topics mirrored
statement: On regional failure healthy regions must continue, critical Fabric topics must have selective cross-region mirrors, and ledger/data services stay available per their managed topology.
rationale: One region's loss must not lose control or outcome history.

verification.check: Disabling a region leaves other cells trading and mirrored P0/P1 topics readable elsewhere.

title: Hot Reflex capacity reserved
statement: Hot Reflex capacity must be reserved with reservations/commitments.
rationale: A replacement VM that cannot be scheduled leaves a venue unserved.

verification.check: Each execution IGM consumes a specific reservation sized to its target; removing reservation_affinity must fail.

title: Warm, data and AI components autoscale
statement: Warm, data and AI components must autoscale where scaling time is compatible with workload behaviour.
rationale: Fixed capacity is wasted on quiet days and short on volatile ones.

verification.check: Plan shows autoscaling bounds for Cloud Run services and data stores.

title: Platform-foundation guardrails project
statement: An org/platform-foundation boundary must hold Org Policy, IAM/PAM patterns, audit sinks, SCC and billing exports, independent of applications.
rationale: Central guardrails must not be editable by application deployers.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: Network-core project
statement: A prod/network-core project must hold NCC hubs, shared DNS, hybrid connectivity, firewall policy and PSC endpoints, separate from workloads.
rationale: Network authority separated from workloads.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: Per-region execution project
statement: Each region must have a prod/exec-<region> project containing the Reflex VPC and Reflex VMs only.
rationale: Smallest blast radius for latency-critical execution.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: Per-region fabric project
statement: Each region must have a prod/fabric-<region> project holding the Fabric VPC, broker VMs, journal disks and archiver identities, so messaging failure cannot reconfigure trading compute.
rationale: Messaging compromise must not reach trading compute.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: Per-region services project
statement: Each region must have a prod/services-<region> project for regional GKE Standard, Redis and regional APIs/sinks.
rationale: Warm services scale independently of Reflex and Fabric.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

notes: KUBERNETES conflicts with ADR 0024; the intent applies to the Cloud Run service plane.

title: Ledger project with its KMS keys
statement: A prod/ledger project must isolate the Spanner ledger/accounting/capital databases and their KMS keys.
rationale: Financial truth isolated from noisy analytics.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: World-model project
statement: A prod/world-model project must hold Spanner Graph/world-model stores, isolated from the ledger.
rationale: Graph query load must not affect the ledger.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: Data project
statement: A prod/data project must hold the GCS archive and knowledge packs, Bigtable, BigQuery and Knowledge Catalog.
rationale: Data governance and analytics boundary.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: AI project
statement: A prod/ai project must hold Vertex/Agent Platform training, registry, agent runtime and GPU/TPU jobs.
rationale: AI permissions and quota separated from financial state.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: Engineering project
statement: A prod/engineering project must hold Cloud Build private pools, Artifact Registry, signing/attestation and the GitOps management cluster.
rationale: Software supply-chain boundary.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: Non-prod mirrors production boundaries
statement: Every nonprod environment must mirror the same logical project/network boundaries at lower scale.
rationale: Architecture parity without production access.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: Plan shows the named project under the right folder holding only the listed resources.

title: No single giant Shared VPC; separated VPCs joined by NCC
statement: The platform must not use one Shared VPC across domains; intentionally separated VPCs are connected through NCC, and Reflex and Fabric networks stay independently governable.
rationale: A single Shared VPC broadens routing and change blast radius.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model

verification.check: No shared-VPC host/service project resource exists; Reflex and Fabric are distinct networks joined only via NCC spokes.

title: Public entry via DNS, global LB, Cloud Armor, CDN, Certificate Manager
statement: User traffic to portal/API must enter through Cloud DNS → Global External Application LB → Cloud Armor → Cloud CDN/Certificate Manager → Cloud Run (or GKE Gateway), with no direct access to internal planes.
rationale: Anycast edge with WAF/DDoS and TLS keeps internal planes unreachable.

verification.check: Plan with public_edge set shows the LB chain with security policy and CDN; a Cloud Run service with public ingress must be refused.

title: Regional warm services via internal LB/mesh with mTLS, never in Reflex path
statement: Regional warm services must be reached through GKE Gateway/regional internal Application LB with Cloud Service Mesh (mTLS, policy, retries/timeouts), and this layer must never be inserted in the Reflex path.
rationale: Mesh policy helps warm services but adds jitter to execution.

verification.check: No execution node sits behind an LB or mesh; warm-service calls use mTLS.

notes: GKE Gateway/Cloud Service Mesh conflict with ADR 0024.

title: VPC-to-VPC via NCC spokes with route filters
statement: VPCs must be connected through Network Connectivity Center VPC spokes with route filters.
rationale: Central route orchestration without flattening networks.

verification.check: Plan shows NCC hub and spokes with include/exclude filters.

title: Dedicated NCC latency mesh hub for Reflex/Fabric
statement: A dedicated NCC mesh hub must export only Reflex/Fabric peer endpoints/ports (narrow prefixes) for cross-region Reflex and Fabric mirror traffic.
rationale: Latency traffic must not share inspection paths.

verification.check: Plan shows a mesh-topology hub with only narrow prefixes exported.

title: Service/data NCC star hub with central inspection
statement: GKE/data/AI/management connectivity must go through an NCC star/hybrid-inspection hub with stronger centralised inspection.
rationale: Non-latency traffic gains inspection.

verification.check: Plan shows a star-topology hub with center/edge groups.

title: Market/custody connectivity via direct path, Interconnect, HA VPN fallback
statement: Venue traffic must use a direct internet path where necessary, Dedicated/Partner Interconnect with Cloud Router for private providers, and HA VPN as fallback — avoiding generic proxies for latency-sensitive venue traffic.
rationale: A generic proxy adds latency and a shared failure for venue traffic.

verification.check: Plan shows interconnect attachment, router and HA VPN; venue egress bypasses the egress proxy.

title: Google APIs reached privately (PGA / PSC)
statement: Spanner, GCS, Bigtable, Artifact Registry and other Google API traffic must stay private via Private Google Access / Private Service Connect where supported.
rationale: Public API paths widen exfiltration and dependency on NAT.

verification.check: Subnets have private_ip_google_access and DNS resolves googleapis to the restricted VIP.

title: Controlled internet egress with static identities, audit, domain controls
statement: Crawler, agent and builder internet egress must go through Cloud NAT or Secure Web Proxy with static egress identities, audit and domain controls; Reflex venue egress is governed separately.
rationale: Uncontrolled egress is an exfiltration and licensing risk.

verification.check: Every NAT uses reserved addresses with logging; egress proxy enforces an allow-list; venue egress has its own rules.

title: Admin access only via IAP/workforce identity/PAM
statement: Administrative access must use IAP, workforce identity and PAM: no public SSH/RDP, and privileged access must be temporary and audited.
rationale: Standing public admin access is the commonest breach path.

verification.check: No machine has an external IP; SSH ingress only from the IAP range; privileged roles granted via PAM entitlements.

title: Reflex compute: C4D/C4, gVNIC/Tier-1, reservations
statement: Reflex VMs must be C4D/C4-class sized by venue/instrument shard, use gVNIC/Tier-1 networking where benchmarked beneficial, and use capacity reservations in production.
rationale: Jitter and replacement capacity decide fill quality.

verification.check: Plan shows c4/c4d, GVNIC, TIER_1 and reservation affinity.

title: Reflex binary under systemd on hardened image, no Kubernetes
statement: The Rust Reflex binary must run directly under systemd on a hardened minimal image, with no Kubernetes or service mesh in the decision loop.
rationale: Orchestrator and sidecar jitter enter the decision loop.

verification.check: Node template has no container runtime; boot image bake installs exactly the required binaries; shielded VM on.

title: OS tuning: isolated CPUs, huge pages, mlockall, IRQ/RPS/XPS
statement: Reflex hosts must apply isolated CPU sets, CPU affinity, huge pages, mlockall, tuned IRQ/RPS/XPS, bounded background services, local scratch SSD and deterministic allocator choices.
rationale: Untuned hosts produce latency outliers nobody can explain.

verification.check: Startup refuses a host lacking isolcpus/hugepages/no-swap; the binary locks memory; IRQ affinity is set.

title: Every OS tuning validated under replay
statement: Each host tuning choice must be validated under replay before adoption.
rationale: An unvalidated tuning can regress latency silently.

verification.check: A replay benchmark comparing tuned vs untuned latency distributions is recorded per change.

title: Reflex state in memory; journal asynchronously to Fabric
statement: Order books, features, compact models, active risk envelope, session/inventory cache, instrument metadata and sequence state must be held in memory, and the journal shipped asynchronously to the Fabric.
rationale: Remote state reads in the loop add latency; a synchronous journal blocks the loop.

verification.check: Cell decides from in-memory state; journal batches reach a fabric partition without blocking a pass.

title: Direct venue sessions with pooled, pre-allocated adapters
statement: Reflex must hold direct FIX/WebSocket/native venue sessions with per-venue connection pools and pre-allocated buffers, with no generic HTTP service between Reflex and venue.
rationale: An intermediary service adds latency and a failure domain to every order.

verification.check: A venue adapter session is opened from the node and orders traverse it without an intermediate HTTP hop.

notes: Real venue sessions conflict with ADR 0003 (paper only) unless against a provider sandbox.

title: Fenced warm standby; never two active owners
statement: A fenced warm standby must run in another zone; activation requires liveness failure plus fencing-epoch and venue-session ownership checks, so two active owners never exist.
rationale: Two active owners double-place orders.

verification.check: For any interleaving of primary/standby liveness, at most one holds the fencing epoch; removing the epoch check must fail.

title: Signed bundle package manager with staged epoch activation
statement: A package manager must download signed model/policy bundles outside the hot loop, verify manifest/KMS signature, stage, health-check, then atomically activate at an epoch boundary.
rationale: A half-applied or unsigned bundle changes behaviour mid-decision.

verification.check: A tampered bundle is refused; a valid one activates only at a pass boundary; activation is atomic.

title: Instant local rollback of activated bundles
statement: The cell must retain the previous bundle locally and roll back instantly without a fetch.
rationale: Waiting for the centre to re-ship prolongs a bad deployment.

verification.check: A rollback restores the previous payload without a fetch and is reachable from an operator/control path.

title: Degraded mode narrows exposure then halts on freshness expiry
statement: On loss of Fabric/service plane/global AI the cell must continue under its last valid envelope, progressively narrow exposure per local policy, and exit/halt when freshness limits expire.
rationale: Halting immediately on any outage is fragile; trading unbounded on stale inputs is dangerous.

verification.check: Cut-off cell's order size falls a step per aged input and stops at envelope expiry with a named refusal.

title: fabricd broker: ingress, routing, replication, fetch
statement: fabricd must provide ingress, partition routing, journal replication and consumer fetch.
rationale: The broker is the single native contract for durable messaging.

verification.check: Produce/fetch round-trip through a real listener; a replica holds every acknowledged record.

notes: Spec says Tokio async runtime and QUIC/mTLS — conflicts with ADR 0001/0011 (no async runtime) and ADR 0002/0009.

title: Broker uses bounded memory
statement: The broker must use bounded memory pools for requests and buffers.
rationale: Unbounded buffering converts overload into an out-of-memory crash.

verification.check: A request over the bound is refused; concurrent connections are capped.

title: fabric-meta: replicated metadata quorum separate from data log
statement: Cluster membership, partition maps, epochs, consumer leases and quotas must be held in a small replicated (Raft) metadata quorum, separated from the data log.
rationale: Metadata on one node is a single point of failure for the cluster.

verification.check: Metadata survives loss of a minority of meta nodes; partition leadership is assigned from it.

notes: 'Mature Raft implementation' is a crate — ADR 0002/0009.

title: fabric-client SDK: idempotent producer, batching, ack profile
statement: The producer/consumer SDK must provide an idempotent producer sequence, batching and an explicit acknowledgement profile.
rationale: Clients without sequence/ack semantics silently duplicate or lose records.

verification.check: SDK producer against fabricd never duplicates on retry and reports quorum only when durable.

title: fabric-schema: registry with immutable IDs and compatibility gates
statement: A schema registry must assign immutable schema IDs and gate compatibility, generating typed Rust bindings.
rationale: Silent schema drift breaks consumers in production.

verification.check: Changing a field without a version bump changes the schema ID and is refused by the gate.

notes: Protobuf/prost would be a new dependency (ADR 0002); in-tree JSON schema shape is used instead.

title: fabric-mirror: selective inter-region replication
statement: fabric-mirror must replicate only configured topics/partitions between regions, with an independent lag budget, never blocking local commit.
rationale: Mirroring that blocks local commit couples regions.

verification.check: A mirrored partition appears in the peer region; stopping the peer does not delay local produce.

title: fabric-archive: immutable segments with manifest, hydrate replay
statement: Closed immutable segments must be archived with manifest/checksum, and replay must be able to hydrate from the archive.
rationale: Without archive hydration history is bounded by broker disk.

verification.check: An archived segment is read back byte-identically; a tampered archive object is refused.

title: fabric-sink-*: destination consumers isolating backpressure
statement: Sinks to Bigtable, BigQuery, Spanner and GCS must isolate destination backpressure from brokers and restart/replay by offset.
rationale: A slow destination must not back up the broker.

verification.check: A stalled sink accumulates lag without slowing produce and resumes from its committed offset.

title: fabric-admin: internal control API/CLI
statement: An mTLS and IAM-bound admin API/CLI must create topics, set quotas and retention, move partitions, drain, and run diagnostics.
rationale: Hand-composed requests during an incident cause incidents.

verification.check: Each admin operation is available, attributed and refused to an unauthorised identity.

title: fabric-observe: metrics/traces/health independent of own topics
statement: The fabric must expose native metrics, traces and health whose liveness does not depend on its own event topics.
rationale: A broker that reports health through itself goes silent exactly when it fails.

verification.check: Health and metrics keep answering when the data plane stops.

title: Fabric transport is QUIC with TLS 1.3/mTLS by default
statement: Producer/consumer and inter-broker sessions must use QUIC over gVNIC with TLS 1.3/mTLS by default (TCP only where benchmarked for bulk mirror flows).
rationale: Plaintext transport lets anything on the path read and replay tokens and records.

verification.check: A plaintext connection is refused; peer identity is proven by certificate.

notes: ADR 0009 prohibits an in-tree TLS stack; QUIC/TLS crates need an ADR.

title: Fabric frame header fields with CRC32C
statement: Each frame header must carry magic/version, message type, schema ID/version, flags, partition, producer ID/epoch, sequence, event ID, source timestamp, logical timestamp, trace ID, payload length and CRC32C.
rationale: Missing header facts force consumers to decode payloads to route, dedupe or verify.

verification.check: Round-trip preserves every field; a bit flip anywhere is detected as corruption.

title: Explicit ordering key, rendezvous leaders, cross-zone followers
statement: Records must be partitioned by an explicit ordering key, partitions assigned to leaders by rendezvous/consistent hashing, and leaders replicate to followers in other zones.
rationale: Implicit ordering loses per-key order; same-zone replicas share a failure.

verification.check: Same key → same partition in produce order; leader assignment stable under broker list order; follower holds every committed batch.

title: RF3 across zones; quorum ack means majority of replicas
statement: Durable profiles must replicate RF3 across zones and a quorum acknowledgement must mean the record survived on a majority of replicas; cross-region mirroring is asynchronous.
rationale: An acknowledgement backed by one disk loses records with that disk.

verification.check: A quorum ack is returned only after ≥2 of 3 replicas fsync; killing any one replica loses no acknowledged record.

title: At-least-once delivery, producer fencing, per-partition replay
statement: Delivery to consumers must be at-least-once; producer epoch/sequence must prevent stale duplicate producers; per-partition offsets must permit replay.
rationale: Without fencing a zombie producer writes after its successor.

verification.check: Superseded producer never appends after successor's first append; replay from any offset returns identical batches.

title: Atomic batches within a partition; sagas across partitions
statement: Append batches must be atomic within one partition, and cross-partition business transactions must be sagas/commands rather than broker transactions.
rationale: Hidden broker transactions couple partitions and fail opaquely.

verification.check: A segment cut at any byte recovers whole batches only; no API appends to two partitions atomically.

title: Backpressure: credit windows, quotas, bounded queues, priority shedding
statement: The fabric must apply credit/window flow control, per-producer quotas, bounded queues and topic priority, sampling/dropping low-priority telemetry before control/outcome traffic is starved.
rationale: Telemetry floods must not starve control and outcomes.

verification.check: Under overload P4 is shed while P0/P1 still commit; quota excess is refused with back-off.

title: Schema compatibility enforced at CI and runtime registration
statement: Backward/forward schema compatibility must be enforced at CI and at runtime registration, so incompatible schemas never reach production topics.
rationale: An incompatible schema in production breaks every consumer at once.

verification.check: CI fails on an incompatible lock change; broker refuses an unregistered schema before append.

title: P0 Critical Control class
statement: P0 topics (risk envelope, model activation, kill/fence, capital grant) must be RF3 quorum, signed, producer-fenced, long-retained with GCS archive, and never intentionally dropped.
rationale: Losing a kill or a grant is a capital-protection failure.

verification.check: A P0 stream refuses a weaker ack, refuses stale-epoch writers, archives, and never sheds.

title: P1 Financial Outcomes class
statement: P1 topics (fills, cancels, position deltas, settlement) must be RF3 quorum with idempotent IDs, long hot retention, immutable archive, and a ledger sink that retries indefinitely.
rationale: A dropped fill is a ledger short for ever.

verification.check: P1 batches are deduplicated, archived, and the ledger consumer retries until applied.

title: P2 Market Journal class
statement: P2 topics (ticks/books/features/decision traces) must be RF3 regional quorum with batch producers, hours/days hot retention by instrument tier, archive to GCS, and throttle mirroring before local ingest.
rationale: Journal overload must degrade mirroring first, not local capture.

verification.check: Under pressure mirror lag grows while local ingest continues.

title: P3 Intelligence/Research class
statement: P3 topics (evidence deltas, episodes, training candidates) must be RF2/3 configurable with throughput batching, replayable, backlog allowed and consumers scaled.
rationale: Research must not be refused for lag.

verification.check: A lagging P3 group is not refused; records remain replayable.

title: P4 Telemetry class
statement: P4 topics must be best-effort or RF2, sampling/dropping oldest under pressure, with direct OTel remaining the primary health path.
rationale: Telemetry must never be the reason control stalls.

verification.check: Under pressure P4 drops oldest; health stays on the direct path.

title: Five brokers per production region across three zones
statement: Each production region must start with five C4D/C4 broker VMs spread across three zones (three minimum).
rationale: Five gives maintenance headroom and reduces correlated quorum pressure.

verification.check: Prod plan shows five broker instances in three zones.

title: Broker journals on persistent Hyperdisk; local SSD transient only
statement: Broker journals must be on persistent Hyperdisk sized for sustained append/read throughput, with local SSD/page cache only for transient acceleration.
rationale: Durability must come from replicated journals, not one local device.

verification.check: Plan shows a separate Hyperdisk journal disk with provisioned throughput.

title: Discovery via Cloud DNS SRV; live map from metadata
statement: Clients must bootstrap from Cloud DNS SRV records (optionally Service Directory) and obtain the live broker/partition map from Fabric metadata.
rationale: Static broker lists break on any change.

verification.check: SRV record resolves; client fetches the partition map before producing.

title: Stable internal broker addresses; no public endpoint
statement: Brokers must have stable internal addresses and no public endpoint; cross-region mirror prefixes are exported only through the latency NCC hub.
rationale: A public broker is an attack surface for control and outcomes.

verification.check: Template has no access_config; addresses are reserved internal; no public forwarding rule.

title: Short-lived workload certificates via CAS; KMS/HSM roots; IAM-mapped identities
statement: Certificate Authority Service must issue short-lived workload certificates, Cloud KMS/HSM must protect signing roots/policy keys, and broker identities must map to GCP service accounts/IAM.
rationale: Long-lived shared secrets cannot be revoked per workload.

verification.check: A broker refuses a client without a valid CAS-issued cert; policy keys are KMS-held.

title: Content-addressed segments to regional GCS landing buckets
statement: Closed segments must be content-addressed and written to regional GCS landing buckets, then lifecycled/copied to durable archive locations per residency policy.
rationale: An archive name that proves content makes tampering visible.

verification.check: An archived object's key is its hash in the regional bucket; lifecycle copies it to the archive bucket.

title: Scale by adding brokers and rebalancing, not reactive autoscale
statement: Brokers must be scaled by adding brokers and rebalancing partitions ahead of peak, never by reactive autoscaling like stateless pods.
rationale: Reactive broker autoscale moves partitions during peak load.

verification.check: Adding a broker triggers a rebalance with no lost record.

title: Rolling broker upgrade never loses quorum
statement: Broker upgrades must proceed one broker at a time — drain leadership, verify replica health, replace image, rejoin — never upgrading enough replicas to lose quorum.
rationale: Parallel upgrades lose quorum and stop control.

verification.check: An upgrade run keeps P0/P1 produce available throughout.

title: Asset/Portfolio brain as autoscaled warm service
statement: The Asset/Portfolio brain must run as a regional warm service backed by Spanner/Bigtable and autoscaled on CPU/custom metrics (HPA).
rationale: Portfolio reasoning scales with load independently of execution.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Capital/Treasury brain writes through controlled services
statement: The Capital/Treasury brain must run as a warm service issuing recommendations/grants and writing authoritative state only through controlled services.
rationale: A brain writing truth directly bypasses the ledger's controls.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Risk brain generates scenarios and envelopes as warm service
statement: The Risk brain must run as a warm regional service producing scenario/stress analysis and risk envelopes.
rationale: Envelope generation needs elastic compute away from the hot path.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Hard pre-trade veto remains local to Reflex
statement: The hard pre-trade risk veto must execute locally inside the Reflex cell; the warm Risk brain only supplies envelopes.
rationale: A remote veto fails open or adds latency when the service plane is degraded.

verification.check: An order exceeding the envelope is refused by the cell with no remote call; removing the local gate must fail the test.

title: Evidence/Provenance service with continuous scoring
statement: An Evidence/Provenance warm service (with Spanner Graph/BigQuery) must continuously score sources and handle contradictions.
rationale: Sources degrade; unscored evidence misleads cognition.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Fabric sinks on dedicated, lag-scaled pools
statement: Fabric consumers/sinks must run on dedicated node pools scaled from consumer lag with destination-specific failure isolation.
rationale: Sink failure must not affect other warm services.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Replay/simulation controllers as batch jobs
statement: Replay/simulation controllers must launch replay shards as batch jobs and compare live vs counterfactual models.
rationale: Replay at scale needs batch compute outside the service plane.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Symbolic reasoners/solvers with no hot-path dependency
statement: Symbolic reasoners and solvers (Z3/OR-Tools/custom Rust) must run on compute-optimised warm capacity with no hot-path dependency.
rationale: A solver in the hot path makes execution latency unbounded.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Crawler/scout workers isolated from trading
statement: Crawler/scout workers must run in isolated pools or Cloud Run jobs with egress, quotas and security posture separate from trading.
rationale: A compromised crawler must not reach trading identities.

verification.check: Scouts run under their own identity and egress path; that identity holds no trading permission.

notes: Cloud Run jobs are an allowed placement, so ADR 0024 is not a blocker.

title: Internal APIs behind internal LB with mTLS/service policy
statement: Regional internal APIs must be entered through an internal Application LB/GKE Gateway with mTLS and service policy.
rationale: Unauthenticated east-west calls let any workload impersonate any other.

verification.check: Plan shows internal LB; calls without client identity are refused.

title: Cloud Run only for burst stateless endpoints, never venue execution
statement: Cloud Run must be used for webhooks/control APIs whose cold-start profile is acceptable and never for venue execution.
rationale: Cold starts in the order path are unbounded latency.

verification.check: No Cloud Run workload can read the venue credential or place orders; only the execution node can.

title: GKE Standard regional clusters spanning zones
statement: Service-plane clusters must be GKE Standard regional clusters with a regional control plane and multi-zone node pools.
rationale: Survives a single-zone loss.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: Separated node pools; research cannot starve control
statement: Node pools must be separated (general, compute, memory, GPU, batch/Spot) with taints/tolerations and PriorityClasses so research jobs cannot starve control workloads.
rationale: Shared capacity lets research starve control.

verification.check: Plan places the workload in the stated GKE pool.

notes: KUBERNETES: GKE placement conflicts with ADR 0024; assess the intent on Cloud Run/Compute Engine.

title: GitOps split: Config Sync, Argo CD, Kargo, Argo Rollouts
statement: Config Sync must own cluster baseline/policy/CRDs, Argo CD applications, Kargo environment promotion, and Argo Rollouts progressive rollout.
rationale: Overlapping controllers fight over the same objects.

verification.check: Each controller is installed and owns only its layer.

notes: ADR 0036 permits the GitOps cluster.

title: Workload Identity + Secret Manager; no long-lived credentials stored
statement: Workloads must authenticate via Workload Identity and read secrets via Secret Manager/CSI mounts; long-lived cloud credentials must not be persisted (e.g. in Kubernetes Secrets).
rationale: A stored long-lived key is a key in every backup and crash dump.

verification.check: Every Cloud Run service mounts secrets as files; SA key creation/upload is refused by org policy.

title: Service mesh only for warm services; never Fabric/Reflex
statement: A service mesh may be used only for warm services with strict timeouts/retries/circuit breaking and mTLS; Fabric and Reflex traffic must never route through mesh sidecars.
rationale: Sidecars add jitter and a failure domain to execution and messaging.

verification.check: No execution/broker machine is in a mesh; warm-service clients enforce timeouts and breakers.

title: World sensing pipeline: egress → scout → parse → evidence → delta
statement: World sensing must flow external source → secure egress → transient scout worker → parse/extract → evidence/provenance → knowledge delta, recording manifest/hash/cursor and writing to graph/Bigtable/memory, with the raw payload discarded.
rationale: Skipping evidence/provenance turns unverified text into knowledge.

verification.check: A fixture source traverses every stage; the output delta carries manifest and provenance and no payload.

title: No general-purpose raw-world-data lake
statement: There must be no general-purpose raw-world-data lake; the durable plane stores only Algorik's compact interpretation plus re-visit metadata.
rationale: A lake raises cost, licensing and privacy exposure.

verification.check: No store holds raw external payloads; a lake-shaped resource fails review.

title: Tier K0 live ambient state
statement: Tier K0 must hold seconds-to-hours of compact derived state in memory/caches and Bigtable.
rationale: Ambient state must be fast and bounded.

verification.check: Derived state is retained in memory with a bounded horizon and spilled to Bigtable.

title: Tier K3 BigQuery holds derived facts, not copied documents
statement: Tier K3 BigQuery tables must contain derived facts/features/outcomes and research datasets, never copied external documents.
rationale: A warehouse of copied documents is a raw lake by another name.

verification.check: Warehouse rows schema has no document-body column.

title: GCS regional landing for tick/internal segments via private APIs
statement: A regional GCS landing store must hold retained tick/internal replay segments and knowledge packs (never raw external corpus), written by fabric-archive over private Google APIs.
rationale: Cheap durable replay foundation without public paths.

verification.check: Plan shows a regional landing bucket; fabricd writes to it via PGA.

title: Durable research/archive with Bucket Lock and versioning
statement: The durable research/archive bucket must receive data by lifecycle from landing and use Bucket Lock/versioning where retention must be immutable.
rationale: Retention that automation can shorten deletes the record an investigation needs.

verification.check: Plan shows locked retention and versioning on the archive bucket.

title: Bigtable multi-cluster with routing app profiles
statement: Bigtable must be multi-cluster with multi-cluster routing for read resilience and app profiles chosen by consistency need, fed by fabric-sink-bigtable.
rationale: A single cluster is a single failure for features and replay indexes.

verification.check: Plan shows ≥2 clusters and app profiles.

title: BigQuery fed by sinks/batch loads, isolated from hot path
statement: BigQuery must be fed via fabric-sink-bigquery or batch loads from GCS and stay isolated from the hot path.
rationale: A warehouse in the hot path makes execution depend on analytics.

verification.check: No edge crate reaches the warehouse; loads come from the fabric/GCS.

title: Knowledge Catalog registers lineage and evidence contracts
statement: Knowledge Catalog must register GCS/BigQuery/Spanner/AI lineage, quality and evidence contracts to ground agents in governed context.
rationale: Agents without governed context act on unknown data.

verification.check: Catalog entries exist for each data product with lineage.

title: Spanner Graph written by world-model workers, serves cognition only
statement: Evidence/world-model workers must write normalised entities/edges into Spanner Graph, whose queries serve cognition and never hot execution.
rationale: Graph queries in execution add unbounded latency.

verification.check: Graph writer exists; no edge crate can reach the graph.

title: AlloyDB for non-financial operational metadata
statement: AlloyDB must hold operational relational metadata/workflow state (admin/research workflow, agent jobs, config history) that is not financial truth.
rationale: Workflow state in the ledger couples it to noisy writes.

verification.check: Workflow state persists via an AlloyDB adapter; ledger tables are absent from it.

title: Dataflow/Dataproc for batch reprocessing only
statement: Dataflow/Dataproc Serverless must be used for large batch reprocessing from durable GCS/BigQuery sources and must not be the primary live fabric consumer path.
rationale: A batch engine as live consumer couples freshness to job scheduling.

verification.check: Batch jobs read GCS/BQ only; no live fabric subscription.

notes: Dataflow/Dataproc pipelines are JVM/Python — conflicts with ADR 0001/0011 (Rust everywhere).

title: Spanner Enterprise Plus multi-region with external consistency
statement: The authoritative ledger/accounting database must be Spanner Enterprise Plus in a multi-region configuration with external consistency.
rationale: Financial truth must survive a region and stay externally consistent.

verification.check: Plan shows edition ENTERPRISE_PLUS and a multi-region config.

title: Separate instances for ledger and world graph
statement: Ledger and world-graph databases must be on separate Spanner instances/databases to avoid noisy-neighbour coupling.
rationale: Graph load must not slow ledger commits.

verification.check: Plan shows distinct instances for ledger and graph.

title: Ledger writer consumes P1 transactionally keyed by event_id
statement: A regional ledger-writer must consume P1 outcome partitions and, in one transaction keyed by event_id, update double-entry postings/positions/cash and record the processed event ID so duplicate delivery is a no-op.
rationale: Non-transactional application loses or doubles fills across a crash.

verification.check: Any redelivery/crash schedule yields balances equal to one clean delivery; process reaches apply from main.

title: Ledger is asynchronous to order placement
statement: The ledger must be asynchronous to order placement so global consistency never slows the hot path.
rationale: A synchronous ledger write puts a multi-region commit in front of every order.

verification.check: No edge crate reaches the storage/ledger crates; the cell places without a ledger call.

title: Spanner leader region chosen by write origin and residency
statement: The Spanner configuration/leader region must be chosen by write origin and legal residency.
rationale: A distant leader adds commit latency; a wrong one breaches residency.

verification.check: Plan sets default_leader with recorded rationale.

title: Spanner managed autoscaling with high minimum; hotspot-safe keys
statement: Spanner must use managed autoscaling with a deliberately high minimum sized for peak close/reconciliation, and keys must be hotspot-safe.
rationale: Autoscaling cannot rescue monotonically increasing keys.

verification.check: Plan shows autoscaling_config with min ≥ sized floor; schema keys not monotonic.

title: Change streams feed analytics only, never the system of record
statement: Spanner change streams/Dataflow may feed BigQuery/reporting and derived caches, which must remain downstream analytics and never the system of record.
rationale: Derived copies treated as truth diverge from the ledger.

verification.check: No component reads balances from a derived copy for a decision.

title: Continuous venue/custody vs ledger reconciliation halts deterministically
statement: Venue/custody truth must be continuously compared with the ledger; discrepancies must raise a P0/P1 Fabric event and can narrow or stop local execution under deterministic policy.
rationale: An unreconciled break compounds with every fill.

verification.check: An injected break emits a fabric event and halts/narrows the cell; removing the trip must fail.

title: Scheduled Spanner backups and PITR
statement: The ledger must have scheduled Spanner backups and point-in-time recovery.
rationale: Without backups a logical corruption is permanent.

verification.check: Plan shows a backup schedule and version_retention_period.

title: Immutable ledger exports and audit manifests to locked GCS
statement: Immutable ledger exports and audit manifests must be written to locked GCS for independent reconstruction.
rationale: Reconstruction evidence must not depend on the database it audits.

verification.check: An export lands in a retention-locked bucket and replays to the same balances.
